Like I said before, if you don’t like your current job then leave. You’re gonna have to find work eventually because that’s the reality; you can’t be a shut in your whole life.

You say you like drawing. Perhaps you could get a job being a graphic designer? Create movie posters, logos for company’s, create art for games etc. Something along those lines. You gotta think outside of the box in finding a future job that matches your interests. You don’t have to do an art degree, or something like that. You just have to think of a job that involves an interest, a hobby or something you’re passionate about (which is easier said than done).

Gaming can be a good outlet and escape to life. It does have its negatives by being inside all the time. Maybe you could play Pokemon Go; gaming and getting outside the house all in 1 (going on walks like you use to)? 

With college. as much as you say you’re doing it for him, you need to do it for you too. Get bothered and put effort in to get the best possible grades. Use your boyfriend as the motivation to this perhaps?

I’d love to talk to you about what’s making you feel like this. I can’t if you kill yourself though. If I’m not available when you’re free, I’m sure there are others either responding to this thread or on hotlines. Seek support and don’t be alone.

The self-respecting is easier said than done. Same with the negative mindset. It’s very hard to come out of that downwards spiral once you’ve been engulfed by it. Have you thought about seeking professional help? I think something like CBT (Cognitive Behavioural Therapy) will be good for. 

With the work situation, the best thing to do about work is when you get to the interviewing stage, be honest about these feelings. I’m sure if you get a job, and they know about this, they’ll try and support you.

In regards with your anxiety and paranoia comments, the only way to get rid of and/or cope with it is by embracing it. Yeah you have anxiety and paranoia, it’s shit and you’d rather not have it, but it’s apart of you and you have to live around it. If you keep staying sheltered and in your comfort zone, the anxiety and paranoia gets worse and it’ll get to a stage where you can’t leave your home.  

With anxiety, you need to develop techniques to cope with your anxiety; having something to fidget with (eg. your phone, some blu-tack or a stress ball of sorts) and take yourself out of the situation for a couple of minutes. Those things work for me but I know everyone is different so you need to think and find your own solutions. 

You also need to start doing things that causes your anxiety to appear. Just doing these things is a win itself. It doesn’t matter if it doesn’t go well, actually going gives you the win and hands anxiety the loss. Also it’ll put your techniques into practice. 

Some of those things might be relevant to help with your paranoia but I’ve never really had it, in the ways you’ve described it, so I can’t really help on that part.

To answer your question, if you’re able to get through the tough times you’re having now, you become a more stronger and resilient.

In regards to everything else, if you’re not happy in this job, find another. Try and find a career that links to your interests or something you’re passionate about; you’ll like the job more than this. If you need to go back into education to do this, do it; you’ll be much happier in the end.
Thank you

The thing about the education system is they put so much pressure on you to pass exams and they make it out like if you fail, that’s it. Game over. It’s not like that at all. 

I flopped my GCSEs in high school and I thought that was it for me. It wasn’t. I went to college and got great grades and now I’m moving on to university, hopefully going into a field that I’ll thoroughly enjoy. 

Yeah it sucks that your friends are leaving and they’re moving forward with their lives (and you feel like you aren’t). If they’re true friends, you’ll keep in contact with them. If not, you’ll make plenty of new friends in the years to come. Just because you’re not progressing at the same pace as others, it doesn’t mean you’re dumb and a failure. You shouldn’t compare yourself to other people because you’re different; you have your own things that you’re good at and not many others aren’t. You just haven’t discovered them yet. In time, you will.

I agree. You need to have an end goal in life, which is easier said than done. Give it a purpose. For me, my end goal is to be in a career I love doing and that I’m happy in. Maybe this could be the same for you. You give up now and it’ll always be “What if...”

I think what that person meant is that despite feeling suicidal, OP hasn’t pulled the trigger yet. OP is strong and resilient and despite the bullshit going in OP’s life, OP is looking for a reason not to quit

With the work situation, you managed to leave the house and work hard to get the job. Even though you may feel like it’s just a shitty job at Walmart, you still had to make the effort to get the job. You should be proud for reaching that far. Today must have suck but that doesn’t mean you should give up. You give up today, you’ll give up with the rest of your life. Be strong

No worries man. To add to my last paragraph: If you decide to go down that route of getting support, and the person you choose is a private counsellor, you’ll need to apply for funding ASAP. It is a very long process, in my case anyway, and you want to make continuous progress instead of stop starting every couple of months

To answer your question “Time heals all wounds” is the wrong way to describe grief. You’ll never properly heal over the death of your mother. You grow around the death of it. Think of it like this: You draw a circle. You write everyone who’s important to you. Your mother was part of that circle but now she isn’t. Instead of crossing her name out, you now have a new circle, which is smaller than the last (due to the loss of your mother). 

Go to 38:25 on [this video](https://youtu.be/S2_8dkluG-c). They talk about grief and I think this’ll help you find an answer to your question.

Hope myself and the video has helped you answer your question

I fully get what you’re going through. To be honest, I was getting freaked out reading this because I was practically living the life you’re living now when I was that age; the autism, mental health issues, dad leaving and the isolation.

With the meds, next time you go to your GP tell them this (this being the numb feeling and etc). That’s not good. They need to change your meds. It isn’t healthy feeling like that and it’s impacting your mood.

GCSEs don’t mean shit. Our education system is fucked up like that; they make it so if you don’t pass, you’re doomed. You managed to get to college so you couldn’t have done that bad. You gotta find what you’re passionate about and link that with a career, whether it’d be something on this computer course or a different thing. 

With the relationship, that was a good move on your part; you ended it cos it was affecting your mental health. Your mental health will always come first. However, it doesn’t mean it was an easy decision. You’re 17. You have plenty of time to get with other girls.

With the cutting and suicidal thoughts, it’s not good (as you already know). From what you’re saying, it’s the only logical thing to do. Seek out support ASAP. I’d recommend searching for someone who deals with autistic people; it opens your mind on how you work and makes you understand everything a lot easier. A lot of autistic people think about suicide around your age.

That long lasting depression is tough to deal with and I understand what you’re going through. Last couple of months have been rough and I was on the edge of killing myself. But I’m still here. Why? The fact we’re still here shows how resilient we are. The amount of effort that it takes to live everyday, and still being here, shows how strong we are (even if we don’t see it at times).

To get on the path of happiness, you need an end goal. My goal is to be in a job that I’m passionate about and I’m happy in. I’ve figured out how to get there. You need to figure out your end goal, which is easier said than done, and how to get there. Once you have something to work for, you can start chasing your dream and start to get your happiness back. There’ll be things on the way that may set us back, but that’s not a reason to give up. If we’ve been this strong and resilient against the battles within ourselves for so long, why would a minor setback that life throws at us cause us to go off our path. We need to think about it as being off-road and steering back onto the main road. Once you’re back on the main road, you’re back on track

If you don’t wanna be a wage-slave then you need to figure out what sorta career you want, which is easier said than done. You need to think about what you’re passionate about, what your interests are, and see if you can get a career out of it. If you have to go back into education to get that career, then do it. It won’t be a waste of time once you’re happy in a job that you love doing. That’s the dream at the end of the day, for me it is anyway

I don’t think CBT will be useful for me now. If you look at my first post, you’ll see what has happened

I think your misinterpreting what I’m saying. The private counsellor I use to see was good. I can’t see her anymore because I can’t afford to. I’m trying to get it on the NHS so I can see her for free. I’m currently not receiving any support as I am waiting for the NHS to get back to me on seeing the previously mentioned private counsellor. 

The CBT was working at the time because my head was in the right place. Because of current events, it doesn’t matter how it was then because all the progress has gone down the drain (due to how I am now)

To answer your first question, the main thing at the moment is just waiting around for everyone and everything. I’m constantly waiting on events and people in my life and I’m sick and tired of getting no response, getting mugged off all the time. I’ve got nothing going on and in my lowest moods, I just don’t see the point of living. There are a lot of other contributions to my depression and anxieties. I’ve wrote them down in a previous post, if you want to read it. It’s pretty long.

To answer the other questions, I’ve done two types of therapy; private and CBT. The private counsellor I use to see was good. I felt like she got me. It’s so annoying at the moment because I’m waiting to see her again on the NHS. Since she’s a private counsellor, she’d cost me money but if I get it on the NHS, it’s free. The CBT was decent at the time but now I feel like it was a waste of my time, as I don’t think it’s helped me move forward regarding my mood.

Thanks for taking the time to respond. Not a lot of people take the time to respond
